description: Bash script that converts Markdown files to Notion-styled PDFs using pandoc

userStories.title: Create Notion-style CSS file
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a CSS file that replicates Notion's document styling for PDF output.
acceptanceCriteria: Create notion.css with system font stack (San Francisco, Segoe UI, sans-serif)
Style headings h1-h6 with Notion-like proportions and weights
Style paragraphs with appropriate line-height and spacing
Style code blocks with monospace font and light gray background
Style inline code with subtle background
Style blockquotes with left border
Style tables with borders and alternating row colors
Style ordered and unordered lists including nested
Style checkboxes for task lists (- [ ] and - [x])
Style callout/admonition blocks
Style horizontal rules
Style links (blue, underline on hover)
Style images with optional captions
Add appropriate page margins for PDF via @media print

userStories.title: Create basic script with argument validation
userStories.description: As a user, I want the script to validate my input so I get helpful error messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Create notionify.sh script with shebang
Accept exactly one argument (markdown filename)
Show usage instructions if no argument provided
Error if file doesn't exist in current directory
Error if file doesn't have .md extension
Exit code 0 for success, 1 for errors
Script is executable (chmod +x)

userStories.title: Add OS detection and pandoc auto-install
userStories.description: As a user, I want pandoc installed automatically so I don't have to manage dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: Detect if pandoc is installed using command -v
Detect OS (macOS vs Linux) using uname
On macOS: install pandoc via Homebrew (install Homebrew first if needed)
On Linux: install via apt-get (Debian/Ubuntu) or yum (RHEL/CentOS/Fedora)
Show informative message during installation
Exit with error if installation fails
Also check and install wkhtmltopdf for PDF generation

userStories.title: Implement PDF conversion workflow
userStories.description: As a user, I want to run notionify myfile.md and get myfile.pdf with Notion styling.
acceptanceCriteria: Store CSS in ~/.notionify/notion.css (create dir if needed)
Copy bundled CSS to ~/.notionify/ on first run
Output PDF has same base name as input (input.md -> input.pdf)
PDF created in current working directory
Call pandoc with: pandoc input.md -t html -o output.pdf -c ~/.notionify/notion.css
Show success message with output filename
Handle pandoc errors gracefully

userStories.title: Create GitHub README
userStories.description: As a potential user, I want clear documentation to install and use the tool.
acceptanceCriteria: Add project title and one-line description
Add installation instructions (clone, chmod +x)
Add usage examples with command syntax
List supported Markdown features
Add requirements/dependencies section mentioning auto-install
Add placeholder for example output screenshot
Add license section (MIT)
